title: Pro-life group calls euthanasia ‘safeguards’ bill the ‘silent death act’
description: OTTAWA ( LifeSiteNews ) — The Canadian Liberal government released a new bill designed to look good on paper by banning euthanasia for those with mental illness. However, in reality, if passed, a pro-life group says the “godless” law will allow people to be euthanized without their consent. Bill C-41, also known as the “safeguards act,” was introduced Tuesday by Liberal Justice Minister Sean Fraser. The bill permanently blocks euthanasia, or Medical Assistance in Dying (MAiD), for those with mental illness. However, Campaign Life Coalition (CLC) warned that it allows a “godless policy” of euthanasia to continue, leaving only doctors and nurses as a check and balance. … As reported by LifeSiteNews, the Catholic Archdiocese of Toronto is urging Canadians to continue to push their MPs to fight against the expansion of euthanasia, notably after the federal government paused an expansion of the practice for the mentally ill, because “work must continue “ to protect the vulnerable with new legislation. Euthanasia in Canada has become so prevalent that recent statistics show the nation recorded more deaths by euthanasia than murders by guns in the United States in 2024. Many provincial governments such as Alberta had protested the planned MAiD expansion. Alberta placed strong limits on assisted suicide, as LifeSiteNews reported .

title: Canadian gov’t claims planned social media ban for minors is constitutional
description: ( LifeSiteNews ) — A proposed social media ban for minors claims the Canadian federal Liberal government is in line with the Charter of Rights, but it may interfere with one’s freedom of expression, it admits. The Liberals’ new Bill C-34 , the Safe Social Media Act, will ban social media use for those under age 16. Executives from Meta (Facebook, Instagram) and Snapchat say app stores should be tasked with age-verifying users, but they admit they don’t know who the ultimate gatekeepers will be. … As reported by LifeSiteNews, Bill C-34 was introduced by Culture Minister Marc Miller on June 10. Besides banning social media for youth, the new bill will also force online platforms to have measures to report credible threats of violence or self-harm to the police. It is expected that the social media ban will be like the one in place in Australia that bans youth under age 16 from having Instagram, TikTok, Facebook, Snapchat, and other platform accounts. However, it has been reported that social media platforms may receive exemptions if they can prove that they meet new safety standards for users, especially minors.
